text:
Maya: FYI Opal Systems (acct OPAL-712) — invoice INV-2025-09 is 34 days overdue for $52,430.20. They replied to the dunning notice and asked to split into multiple payments. Copy of their email below.

Juan: Got it. Do they have ACH or card on file?

Maya: ACH only, procurement said. Email excerpt: "We can do three installments, starting next Monday. Can you confirm dates and process for ACH?"

Chris: Proposed schedule (finance suggestion):
```
- 2025-05-05: $15,729.06 (30%)
- 2025-06-05: $15,729.06 (30%)
- 2025-07-05: $20,972.08 (40%)
```
If first payment posts we remove the temporary service hold.

Liz: Ok from CSM side if they sign the addendum and complete ACH mandate. I'll prep the short addendum.

Maya: CollectionsBot sent dunning level 2 on 2025-04-10 :email:, they replied same day asking for the split.

Chris: We need approval for the staggered timeline (payments >30 days apart). @Juan please confirm Sales is ok to allow release on first payment only and to keep interest clause for late installments (1.5% monthly per SOW).

Juan: Sales approves releasing service after payment 1. Interest clause is fine. Require CSM + Finance on the addendum.

Maya: I'll reissue the invoice with the addendum attached and include ACH instructions. Will mark the account so collections knows to clear hold on receipt of payment 1.

CollectionsBot: Automated note: next follow-up scheduled in 7 days if no payment received.

Chris: If payment 1 not received by 2025-05-12 escalate to Manager for potential write-off discussion.

Maya: Sending addendum & ACH form to procurement now. Snippet of email I sent: "Attached: installment addendum + ACH form. Please confirm ACH setup and expected payment date by EOD Friday. On receipt of first payment we will remove the temporary service hold. — Maya, Finance"

Liz: I'll ping the procurement contact tomorrow morning to confirm receipt.

Chris: Logged OPAL-712 in collections queue, tagging for 30-day checkpoint.

Juan: Thanks team. Keep me posted. :thumbsup:
